nodes.label: LoRA / QLoRA 4-bit Fine-tuning
nodes.author: null
nodes.rationale: 4-bit NF4 quantization (rank=16, alpha=32) used to enable fine-tuning on a single consumer GPU (RTX 4090 Laptop) while keeping memory usage within 16 GB VRAM.

nodes.label: Dataset v3-rebuild (99K)
nodes.rationale: Previous v3 dataset (52K) was missing Path Traversal and CSRF due to renamed PayloadsAllTheThings folder names; fixing folder mappings added ~46K examples. Doubled size improves category coverage, especially CSRF which had 0 training examples before.

nodes.label: GGUF Export for llama.cpp
nodes.rationale: GGUF format enables CPU/embedded inference via llama.cpp, targeting low-resource embedded Linux systems. HuggingFace Transformers inference is ~800ms which is the pre-optimization baseline.

nodes.label: Python 3.12 ML Environment
nodes.rationale: Post-reinstall, python3 maps to Python 3.14 which lacks the ML stack; all scripts must explicitly use python3.12 where torch, transformers, peft, trl, etc. are installed.

nodes.label: Proxy as Data Factory (Future Strategy)
nodes.rationale: Rather than generic benign-traffic datasets (which carry app/era bias like CSIC), capturing real traffic via a local proxy (e.g. DVWA/bWAPP + Burp Logger) ensures the same HTTP envelope for both ALLOW and BLOCK, breaking User-Agent/cookie shortcut bias.

nodes.label: v4 Improvement Plan
nodes.rationale: Incremental plan: Group 1 removes ###END### token (design cleanliness), Group 2 strengthens JWT/GraphQL weak categories, Group 3 fixes CSIC SQL bias via subsampling.

nodes.label: CSIC Envelope Bias (Konqueror UA / JSESSIONID)
nodes.rationale: All CSIC examples share the same Konqueror User-Agent and JSESSIONID cookie pattern, risking the model learning to detect attacks by envelope rather than payload content.
